Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY DILG OPINION NO. JUN 2 S VICE MAYOR LEONILO 1. YAP Plaridel, Bulacan Dear Vice Mayor Yap: 102 s. 2010 This refers to your request for legal opinion on the following issues, to wit: 1. Can an alleged act committed during the previous term of office of re-elected Barangay Kagawad and a former Punong Barangay be the basis of a complaint during their present term? Can an appealed case constituting an act committed during such previous term still proceed at this time?; 2. If the reply in the above query is in the negative, can the respondent elective barangay official be reinstated to office or does he automatically assume the office?; 3. Can the municipal mayor, upon the recommendation of the Sangguniang Bayan, remove from office an elective barangay official pursuant to the aforesaid administrative case?. Anent the three issues, please be informed that we had already an occasion to answer similar queries in DILG Opinion No. 52 series of 2000, dated 09 June 2000. In the said opinion, we opined that any misconduct committed by an elective official during the previous term cannot be used to initiate an administrative complaint against the same re-elected official during his present term of office. With regard to the second query, which is quite vague, if the decision of the administrative disciplinary authority penalizing the respondent local elective official with removal from the service had become final and executory before the election, then the principle of condonation for a misconduct during a prior term will not apply. On the other hand, if the said adverse decision against the respondent was not yet final and executory on the day of election as for instance there was a timely and pending appeal on said date, then the principle of condonation will apply. The right of the respondent to hold the office will therefore depend on his situation as discussed above.

With regard to your third query, we answer in negative. Neither the municipal mayor nor the sangguniang bayan has the power to remove from office an elective barangay official pursuant to an administrative case. Attached herewith is a photocopy of DILG Opinion No. 52 series of 2000, for your ready perusal. We hope this settles your concern. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: A Lega/ Serwce:LD/12/e//en . JESUS DOQ Director III
